title: My first real assisted project progress
author: UFCFan918
selftext:
Hey everyone!

So I've been developing a game called **Desktop Sports**, and it's finally reached the point where it's playable. With that being said It's still in Pre-Alpha, so there's plenty left to add, fix, and polish, but I'd love to start getting feedback from people outside my own testing. 

The idea behind this game is quite simple, the Nintendo Switch has wii sports, but PC doesn't really have anything like that, Thus I felt the need to begin a journey of creating something. 

I have found using Rosebud AI among other AI programs have significantly improved my ability to address and reimagine my line of thinking and progression. AI has opened doors I didn't think we're possible until recently.

Current features:

* 🎮 13 mini-games
* 👥 1–4 player support
* 🏆 Steam leaderboards for every mini-game
* 🌎 Offline play
* 🔥 5 difficulty levels
* ⭐ 5 prestige levels with unlockables
* 🎵 Unlockable menu music

Future plans include adding more unique mini games, more unique unlockables, as well as unique prestige and avatar icons.

You can try it right now for free by using the link above.

Feedback/thoughts mean everything!



*(I posted this yesterday but ive since deleted that post and now included a video of the game)*



**Below is a direct link to the game for you to try for free! No signup etc needed.** 

[https://rosebud.ai/play/rgb-rage-arcade](https://rosebud.ai/play/rgb-rage-arcade)

comments.author: heavyc-dev
comments.body:
I don’t get the point of this. What would drive someone to want to play this? It’s just super generic copies of simplistic existing games. If you’re just making this for yourself I get that but why would someone else want this? I’m not trying to be a douche I just don’t understand it

That all being said under the assumption it’s not just an ad for that site

replies.author: UFCFan918
replies.body:
Fair point and great question! Allow me to pick your brain. 

First off, I think it could be a fun party game if I do it properly. None of the games are ready yet, they need lots of work and honestly a few need reimagining.  The goal/concept I'm going for is this, it would essentially be a game where people can compete on skill games worldwide and have it tracked via Steam leaderboards and offline/local.   

Some of the mini-games are essentially clones, but that's the point, my game allows you to compete with others playing those simplistic games. I'm adding a score system, a timer, and special effects to generic games and unique ones, then the users play them and attempt to get a high score on them. 

Id sell something like this for $1 or $2 - Just as a fun party game. 

I would like to add that I'm far off from my end goal - And the project could look entirely different by the time I'm done. I feel the concept for this game works but the game needs more identity and work in general.
